deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is assessing Washnitzer–Monsky (W.M.) formal cohomology as a forerunner of crystalline cohomology, in notes for his Nov–Dec 1967 'laïus' on crystals. The previous page lists formal defects. The method uses only de Rham complexes of liftings, so it is in practice limited to smooth X_0. It gives no handle on liftings of morphisms, and hence no dévissage. As a result, W.M. had not proved the most basic formal properties: finite generation of H^i_WM(X) over W, and hence no duality or Künneth theorem.

This page finishes that sentence. In parentheses it then concedes a positive point. As Grothendieck understands it, W.M. do succeed in giving a Lefschetz–Weil expression for the zeta function of a smooth projective scheme over a finite field. They do this by showing that the Frobenius operators on their H^i(X) are trace-class operators. He remarks that this formalism seems close to Dwork's, 'which I do not know'.

He then opens §3, 'Heuristique de W.M. — Relations avec mes idées de Gauss-Manin'. Item 1 says the invariance statement of W.M. (independence of the cohomology from the chosen lifting) is surprising at first sight.

The next page explains the heuristic. Embed X_0 in a large modular family Y → M, with M of finite type over S = Spec W. Different sections g of M over S give different liftings X_g. Put K = Rf_*(Ω^•_{Y/M}). Then Rf_{g*}(Ω^•_{X_g/S}) ≅ g^*K, and in good cases R^i f_{g*} ≅ g^*H^i. The Gauss–Manin connection on the H^i over the p-adically connected base then identifies the de Rham cohomologies of the various liftings. This is the standard motivating heuristic for crystals: de Rham cohomology of a lifting depends only on X_0, up to canonical isomorphism, because of the Gauss–Manin connection, i.e. a crystal structure.
errors: The parenthetical description of the W.M. trace formula is approximate, and Grothendieck himself flags his uncertainty. Monsky's Lefschetz fixed-point/trace formula works for smooth affine varieties via dagger (weakly complete) algebras. It uses Dwork-type nuclear (completely continuous) operators at the cochain level, essentially the inverse Frobenius/ψ operator together with duality. Finite-dimensionality of MW cohomology was not known in general then. So 'Frobenius on H^i(X) are trace-class operators' is a loose summary rather than an exact statement.
W.M. cohomology is natively a theory for smooth affine varieties. Speaking of 'schéma projectif et lisse' slightly conflates it with the then-hoped-for global theory.

ideas.what: Critique of Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology: lack of finiteness over W, and hence no duality or Künneth; limited to smooth varieties; no functoriality for liftings of morphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Monsky–Washnitzer (formal/dagger) cohomology and its shortcomings, later remedied by rigid cohomology (Berthelot) and finiteness theorems (Berthelot, Kedlaya, Mebkhout)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Monsky–Washnitzer 1968; finiteness by Berthelot 1997, Mebkhout 1997, Kedlaya 2006
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (IHES notes 1966, in Dix exposés 1968), introduction

ideas.what: Lefschetz trace formula for the zeta function via Frobenius acting as a nuclear operator, linked to Dwork's method.

Heuristic for invariance of de Rham cohomology of liftings: embed X_0 in a versal/modular family Y/M over W; base change Rf_{g*}Ω ≅ g^*Rf_*Ω^•_{Y/M}; the Gauss–Manin connection identifies the fibres over different W-sections.
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin connection / crystalline nature of de Rham cohomology of liftings
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a preparatory draft of material that appears essentially verbatim in spirit in Grothendieck's published 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes': the W.M. critique and the Gauss–Manin heuristic. The only small personal detail is his admission that he did not know Dwork's formalism.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads 'ni d'un théorème de dualité, ni de Künneth' (continuing '…donc sans doute' from the previous page), not 'un cas de théorème de dualité, ou de Künneth'.
Heading: the crossed-out '2)' and the inserted 'Heuristique de W.M.' are joined by a brace to 'Relations avec mes idées de Gauss-Manin'.
